{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "She went back up the slip more slowly than she had come down it, and this time she watched the water. The tide was well out now. The mud between the posts had gone from shining to dull, and the gulls had lifted off it in ones and twos and settled again farther out, where the channel still held a thread of grey.

At the top she stopped and looked at the house. From here the door was a black slot in the whitewash. She had left it open. She could not remember doing it, but there it was, and the wind was going in.

The chart lay where she had found it, weighted at one corner with the salt jar. She had not touched it yet. She had made tea instead, which was the sort of thing her mother would have done, and she had known it while she did it and done it anyway.

Now she stood over the table and read it the way you read a face across a room. The coast was hers, the point and the bay and the two reefs off the headland that everyone knew and nobody bothered to mark. But the soundings were new. Someone had been out with a lead line in the last month, in water she had not thought anyone still cared about.

And there, in the lee of the far reef, a pencilled cross. No name. No depth. Just the cross, and beside it, small and careful, a date three days from now.

She put the kettle back on. Then she took her boots off, sat down, and began to think about what she would need."}
